title: Which crop is best for black soil during Kharif season?
question: Which crop is best for black soil during Kharif season?
content: Cotton and Soybean are the most suitable crops for black clay soil during the Kharif season due to the soil's excellent water retention and mineral composition.

title: What crops grow well in sandy loam soil with low water availability?
question: What crops grow well in sandy loam soil with low water availability?
content: Groundnut, Bajra (Pearl Millet), Mothbean, Chickpea, and Mustard perform extremely well in sandy loam soils with low water requirements.

title: How to increase soil organic carbon naturally?
question: How to increase soil organic carbon naturally?
content: Incorporate green manure crops (Dhaincha, Sunnhemp) into the soil before flowering, apply well-rotted Farmyard Manure (FYM) or Vermicompost @ 4-5 tonnes/acre, and practice zero-tillage or stubble retention.
source: ICAR Indian Institute of Soil Science

title: How to treat acidic soil with low pH?
question: How to treat acidic soil with low pH?
content: Apply agricultural Lime (Calcium Carbonate / Dolomite) @ 200-400 kg/acre based on soil test recommendation 2-3 weeks prior to sowing. Wood ash and organic compost also help neutralize soil acidity.

title: When is the best time to apply Urea to wheat crops?
question: When is the best time to apply Urea to wheat crops?
content: Apply 50% of the total Urea as a basal dose during sowing, 25% at Crown Root Initiation (CRI stage, 21 days after sowing), and the remaining 25% during late tillering stage before irrigation.

title: Why is Sulphur important for oilseed crops like Mustard and Groundnut?
question: Why is Sulphur important for oilseed crops like Mustard and Groundnut?
content: Sulphur is a key component of oil-synthesizing enzymes and sulfur-containing amino acids (Methionine, Cysteine). Applying 20-30 kg Sulphur/acre increases oil content in mustard and groundnut seeds by 3-5%.

title: What are the most critical irrigation stages for wheat?
question: What are the most critical irrigation stages for wheat?
content: The most critical stage is Crown Root Initiation (CRI stage at 20-25 days after sowing). Missing CRI irrigation can cause up to 30% yield loss. Other key stages are tillering, flowering, and milk/grain filling.

title: How does Drip Irrigation help in Sugarcane and Banana cultivation?
question: How does Drip Irrigation help in Sugarcane and Banana cultivation?
content: Drip irrigation saves 40-50% water, enables precise daily fertigation (liquid fertilizer application), reduces weed proliferation between rows, and increases crop yield by 20-35%.

title: How to protect vegetable crops from heatwave conditions?
question: How to protect vegetable crops from heatwave conditions?
content: Irrigate crops in the evening hours, maintain straw or organic mulch on soil beds, erect green shade nets over nursery beds, and spray 1% Potassium Nitrate to reduce heat stress.

title: What to do if there is waterlogging after heavy rainfall?
question: What to do if there is waterlogging after heavy rainfall?
content: Open surface drainage channels immediately to drain standing water within 24 hours. Once standing water recedes, apply a foliar spray of 1% Urea + 0.5% Zinc Sulphate to restore root metabolism.

title: How to prepare Jeevamrutha for organic crop nutrition?
question: How to prepare Jeevamrutha for organic crop nutrition?
content: Mix 10 kg fresh cow dung, 10 liters cow urine, 2 kg jaggery, 2 kg pulse flour (besan), and 200 grams fertile soil in 200 liters water. Stir twice daily and ferment for 48-72 hours. Apply 200 liters per acre with irrigation water.
source: National Centre of Organic and Natural Farming (NCONF)

title: How to control sap-sucking pests like Aphids and Whiteflies organically?
question: How to control sap-sucking pests like Aphids and Whiteflies organically?
content: Spray Neem Oil (10,000 ppm) @ 5 ml/liter water mixed with 1 ml liquid soap. Install yellow sticky traps @ 10-15 per acre. Spray Agniastra or Dashparni Kashayam for severe infestations.

title: What is crop rotation and why is it beneficial?
question: What is crop rotation and why is it beneficial?
content: Crop rotation is growing different crop types (e.g. Cereal followed by Legume) sequentially on the same plot. It breaks pest/disease cycles, restores soil nitrogen via pulse root nodules, and prevents soil nutrient depletion.

title: How to determine the right moisture level for grain storage?
question: How to determine the right moisture level for grain storage?
content: Grains should be sun-dried until moisture drops below 12% for cereal grains (Wheat, Paddy, Maize) and below 9-10% for oilseeds and pulses. Grains should crack sharply when bitten between teeth without softness.
source: Food Corporation of India (FCI) Quality Standards

title: What is e-NAM and how does it help farmers get better prices?
question: What is e-NAM and how does it help farmers get better prices?
content: e-NAM (National Agriculture Market) connects mandis across India electronically. Farmers get produce quality tested at APMC assaying labs, list their lot online, and receive competitive bids from buyers nationwide, eliminating local cartel price suppression.
